Mr. Kalu Ram Bhati, representing the convict-petitioner, submitted that the learned District Parole Advisory Committee, Bhilwara has committed an error of law in rejecting petitioner's application for first parole under the Rajasthan Prisoners Release on Parole Rules, 1958 (herein referred to "the rules of 1958).

recommending parole is that the victim and her family members living in the same village where the petitioner belongs to, and there may be chances of further crime.

He further cited a precedent where, under similar circumstances, a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court granted parole vide order dated 28.02.2024 passed in D.B. Criminal Writ Petition No.148/2024 (Sahi Ram Vs. State of Rajasthan & Ors.).
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Anil Joshi, learned Government Advocate cum Additional Advocate General opposed the grant of parole by contending that petitioner is serving a sentence pursuant to his conviction under provisions of Section 302 and 376 of IPC and since he has committed grave offence, he be not released on parole.
It was argued that releasing the convict- petitioner on parole would have negative bearing on social and psychological well-being of the victim, who resides in the same village. .
4. Mr. Bhati at this juncture submitted that the convict- petitioner would spend his time of parole at the place which is away from the victim's place of residence.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
6.
The convict has already undergone a sentence of about 05 years.
Moreover, the adverse report of the Social Justice and Welfare Department, Bhilwara, cannot, in itself, be grounds for refusing parole.
It is well settled that parole is a device for reformation of a criminal for his rehabilitation in society.
The [2024:RJ-JD:33571-DB] (3 of 4) [CRLW-1534/2024] object of parole can't be frustrated on the basis of vague and ill- founded reasons.

7. The Court acknowledges that the presence of the convict- petitioner could potentially have an adverse impact on the victim's mental well-being, forcing her to revisit the trauma and be reminded of the incident she may be striving to forget.
However, a balance must be struck between the victim's safety and emotional well-being and the statutory rights of the accused.
This Court opines that such a balance can be achieved if the accused spends his parole period at a location distant from the victim's residence.

8. In light of the limited submissions made and on perusal of the peculiar factual matrix, this petition is allowed and the petitioner - Narayan @ Ram Narayan S/o Shri Nainu Ram is directed to be released on first parole of 20 days, strictly in accordance with the provisions of Parole Rules after ensuring its strict compliance as required before his release upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sound and solvent sureties of Rs.25,000/- each (out of which one shall be of accused-petitioner's close family member) to the satisfaction of Superintendent, Central Jail, Ajmer.

The Superintendent, Central Jail concerned will give a date for surrender of convict and shall also be at liberty to impose other reasonable and adequate conditions to ensure his return to the State custody after availing the parole.

9. This Court directs that if the petitioner, during the period in which he is released on parole,
indulges in any kind of offence or/ and any report is lodged against him of any offence, then, in such event, the parole granted to him shall stand cancelled.
